manifest.name: Cloud Storage Migration
manifest.summary: Migrate local attachments to cloud storage
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: Cloud Storage Migration Report (_auto=False SQL view, list-only)

relations: ir.attachment -> cloud storage URL (_generate_cloud_storage_url from cloud_storage module)
ir.attachment -> cloud storage upload endpoint (requests.Session.request, method/url from _generate_cloud_storage_upload_info)

models._description: Adds migration progress field and model-selector One2many fields wired to ir.config_parameter via config_parameter attr

behavioral_notes.observation: _migrate_local_to_cloud_storage(session) validates that the attachment type is 'binary' and store_fname is set (raises ValidationError otherwise). It calls self._full_path(self.store_fname) to get the filesystem path, then self._generate_cloud_storage_url() (from the cloud_storage module) to get the target URL, and self._generate_cloud_storage_upload_info() to get {method, url, headers, response_status}. The local file is opened as binary and uploaded via session.request(method, url, data=f, headers=headers, timeout=(10, 30)) — the requests.Session is passed in by the caller to allow HTTP keep-alive across batch iterations. On non-matching response status, a ValidationError is raised. On success, the attachment is written with type='cloud_storage', raw=False, and mimetype is explicitly preserved (it is set in the same write call to prevent Odoo from recomputing it from the binary).

behavioral_notes.element: ir_attachment.py — _cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage: cron entry point, HTTP vs. cron-worker split
behavioral_notes.observation: _cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage (decorated @assert_log_admin_access) is the cron entry point. It reads migration parameters from ir.config_parameter: cloud_storage_provider (must exist), cloud_storage_min_file_size (from cloud_storage module), cloud_storage_migration_max_file_size (default 1 GB), cloud_storage_migration_max_batch_file_size (default 10 GB), and comma-separated model lists cloud_storage_migration_message_models / cloud_storage_migration_all_models (validated against env registry). If neither model list is populated, UserError is raised. A critical branch: if odoo.http.request is truthy (i.e. the call arrives from an HTTP worker via the 'Manually Run' button), the method immediately calls cron._trigger() to reschedule and returns — no upload happens on the HTTP worker. Only a cron-server worker (where request is None) performs actual uploads. This prevents file-upload I/O from blocking HTTP request workers.

behavioral_notes.element: ir_attachment.py — _cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage: SQL query and cursor-level progress tracking
behavioral_notes.observation: The main loop selects one attachment at a time using a raw SQL query on ir_attachment (LEFT JOIN message_attachment_rel to detect mail-linked attachments, LEFT anti-join to documents_document if that module is installed). Filters: type='binary', url IS NULL, res_id IS NOT NULL, res_field IS NULL, store_fname IS NOT NULL, file_size BETWEEN min_file_size AND max_file_size, create_date < now() - 7 days (recent attachments excluded to avoid disrupting ongoing business operations), id between 0 and max_attachment_id (a stable ceiling set once at start). Progress is tracked via ir.config_parameter 'cloud_storage_migration_min_attachment_id': commit_min_attachment_id(attachment.id) directly executes UPDATE ir_config_parameter SET value=%s to bypass ORM cache invalidation (ormcache), then calls env['ir.cron']._commit_progress(1) to commit the transaction. On upload failure, env.cr.rollback() is called to undo only the write ({type,raw}) without losing the progress update (which was already committed by commit_min_attachment_id).

behavioral_notes.element: cloud_storage_migration_report.py — cloud.storage.migration.report: SQL view and computed migration flags
behavioral_notes.observation: cloud.storage.migration.report is a _auto=False model (no managed table). init() drops and recreates a PostgreSQL VIEW joining ir_attachment (grouped by res_model with SUM/MAX/COUNT of file_size, split into 'message' and 'all' aggregates) with ir_model (to get the ORM id as the record id). The view only counts type='binary' attachments with res_id IS NOT NULL, res_field IS NULL, and non-null file_size/res_model. _compute_message_to_migrate and _compute_all_to_migrate read ir.config_parameter 'cloud_storage_migration_message_models' / 'cloud_storage_migration_all_models' to flag which models are currently scheduled. get_progress() computes migration percent as min_attachment_id * 100 // max(max_attachment_id, min_attachment_id) reading max from ir.config_parameter and min via direct cr.execute to avoid ORM cache interference.

behavioral_notes.element: res_config_settings.py — CloudStorageMigrationSettings: settings UI wiring and action
behavioral_notes.observation: CloudStorageMigrationSettings inherits res.config.settings and adds cloud_storage_migration_progress (Integer, populated in get_values from report.get_progress()), cloud_storage_migration_message_model_ids (One2many to ir.model, inverse=_inverse_cloud_storage_migration_message_model_ids), and cloud_storage_migration_all_model_ids (One2many to ir.model, inverse=_inverse_cloud_storage_migration_all_model_ids). The inverses write comma-joined model names into the cloud_storage_migration_message_models / cloud_storage_migration_all_models config_parameter Char fields. get_values() reads these params back, validates model names against env, and issues Command.set to hydrate the One2many from ir.model.search. action_open_cloud_storage_migration_configurations returns an act_window on ir.config_parameter filtered to the 7 migration-related parameter keys, providing a power-user escape hatch to the raw parameters.

it_architecture.application: cloud_storage_migration (IT operations tool: migrates existing local binary ir.attachment records to cloud storage via a cron-driven batch upload loop, with a settings UI and a SQL-view report)
data_objects: cloud.storage.migration.report (_auto=False SQL view: attachment stats by model + migration flags)
res.config.settings (inherit: progress display, model-scope selectors, raw-param escape hatch)
logical_data_erm: ir.attachment.res_model -> ir.model (report view JOIN on model name)
ir.attachment.id LEFT JOIN message_attachment_rel.attachment_id (to identify mail-linked attachments)
ir.attachment.id LEFT anti-JOIN documents_document.attachment_id (excluded if documents module present)
information_flows: depends: cloud_storage (provides _generate_cloud_storage_url, _generate_cloud_storage_upload_info, DEFAULT_CLOUD_STORAGE_MIN_FILE_SIZE, res.config.settings view extension point)
trigger path (HTTP): user clicks 'Manually Run' -> _cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage detects request truthy -> cron._trigger() -> returns immediately (no upload on HTTP worker)

trigger path (cron): cron worker -> _cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage -> raw SQL SELECT loop -> per-attachment _migrate_local_to_cloud_storage -> requests.Session.request PUT/POST -> ir.attachment write(type='cloud_storage')
progress tracking: commit_min_attachment_id -> direct UPDATE ir_config_parameter -> env['ir.cron']._commit_progress(1) commits transaction
failure path: ValidationError or any Exception -> env.cr.rollback() -> skip attachment -> continue loop
timeout path: time.monotonic() > end_time (half of limit_time_real_cron or limit_time_real) -> break -> cron._trigger() to reschedule
batch-size path: total_file_size + file_size >= max_batch_file_size -> break -> cron._trigger()
report path: cloud.storage.migration.report SQL view -> Settings > Cloud Storage Migration > Attachments Report (list view)
settings path: res.config.settings.get_values -> cloud.storage.migration.report.get_progress() + ir.config_parameter model lists -> populate form
settings-write path: _inverse_*_model_ids -> comma-joined model names -> ir.config_parameter (cloud_storage_migration_message_models / all_models)

capabilities: Migrate existing local binary attachments (ir.attachment type='binary') to cloud object storage, changing type to 'cloud_storage'
Scope migration by model (message-linked attachments only, or all attachments per model) configured via Settings UI
Batch migration with configurable size limits (per-file min/max, per-run max_batch_file_size) and time-budget-aware cron (half of limit_time_real_cron)
Progress tracking via ir.config_parameter watermark (min_attachment_id / max_attachment_id) and a Settings progressbar
Resumable, idempotent migration: watermark-based cursor is committed before each upload so a crash does not re-upload already-migrated attachments
HTTP-worker safety: 'Manually Run' button redirects to cron scheduler without performing I/O on the HTTP worker
Exclusion rules: attachments created within the last 7 days, those linked to documents.document, those with no res_id or with res_field set, and size outliers are all filtered out
Attachment report (cloud.storage.migration.report SQL view) showing per-model attachment counts and sizes with current migration scheduling status
value_streams: Admin-configure stream: admin sets model scope in Settings (message models / all models) -> ir.config_parameter updated -> cron enabled

Cron-migrate stream: cron fires -> raw SQL selects next eligible binary attachment -> _migrate_local_to_cloud_storage -> upload to cloud -> write type='cloud_storage' -> watermark committed -> loop until timeout or batch exhausted -> cron._trigger() reschedules
Progress-monitor stream: admin opens Settings -> get_values calls get_progress() -> progressbar shows min/max watermark ratio -> Attachments Report list view shows per-model stats and migration flags
information_concepts: ir.attachment (the migrated entity: type transitions binary -> cloud_storage)
cloud.storage.migration.report (read-only SQL view: per-model attachment stats)
ir.config_parameter (runtime state: watermark ids, model lists, size limits)
policies: Uploads are performed only on cron-server workers, never on HTTP request workers (request-truthy guard in _cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage)
Attachments created within the last 7 days are excluded (create_date < now() - 7 days) to protect ongoing business operations
Attachments linked to documents.document are excluded when that module is installed
Attachments with res_field set (binary field storage) or no res_id are excluded
Only attachments with stored filename (store_fname IS NOT NULL) and within the configured size window are eligible
The migration cursor (min_attachment_id) is committed before each upload attempt — upload is idempotent across restarts
Failed uploads trigger env.cr.rollback() and log a warning; the cursor is already committed so the failed attachment is skipped in subsequent runs
The cron job interval is set to 9999 months by default (effectively disabled until triggered manually or via _trigger)
stakeholders: System administrator configuring and monitoring the migration from Settings
Cron server worker (performs the actual I/O-bound upload batches)
Cloud storage provider (receives PUT/POST requests from requests.Session)
Odoo cloud_storage module (provides URL/upload-info generation and the provider abstraction)
metrics: Migration progress percentage: min_attachment_id * 100 // max_attachment_id (shown as progressbar in Settings)
Per-model attachment counts and sizes (cloud.storage.migration.report: message_count, all_count, message_sum_size, all_sum_size in MB)
total_file_size per cron run (logged at batch-size cutoff)

classification.rationale: cloud_storage_migration is a data-infrastructure migration tool with no customer-facing value chain activity: it moves binary blobs from local disk to cloud object storage. It owns no business model of its own (cloud.storage.migration.report is a read-only SQL view for admin monitoring; ir.attachment and res.config.settings are inherited), has 0 routes, application=False. Porter support; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support' (IT infrastructure capability). APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the correct category: this is IT operations/storage management — managing the IT infrastructure (object storage tier) that all other application modules depend on. 13.0 (Business Capabilities) was rejected as this is not a business-process capability; it is a one-time IT infrastructure migration operation.

standard_capabilities: Cron-driven batch migration of local binary ir.attachment records to cloud object storage (type 'binary' -> 'cloud_storage')
Two migration scopes: message-linked attachments only, or all attachments per model (configured as model lists in Settings)
Configurable per-file size window (cloud_storage_min_file_size to cloud_storage_migration_max_file_size) and per-run batch ceiling (max_batch_file_size)
Time-budget-aware cron with automatic rescheduling (cron._trigger()) on timeout or batch exhaustion
Resumable watermark-based progress tracking via ir.config_parameter (min_attachment_id cursor committed before each upload)
HTTP-worker safety: 'Manually Run' button in Settings redirects immediately to cron scheduler
Attachment report SQL view (cloud.storage.migration.report) with per-model counts, sizes, and migration scheduling flags
Exclusion of recent attachments (< 7 days), documents.document-linked files, res_field binary fields, and size outliers
typical_fits: Post-deployment migration of legacy on-premises Odoo attachment binaries to a cloud provider already configured in the cloud_storage module
Incremental zero-downtime migration during live production (cron runs in background, HTTP workers unaffected)
Admin-controlled scoping: migrate only email-attachment-heavy models first (e.g. mail.message) then expand
common_gaps: No reverse migration (cloud -> local): the module is one-directional only
No parallel upload workers: the cron is single-threaded (one attachment per loop iteration, one requests.Session)
Failed attachments are silently skipped after rollback — no retry queue or failed-attachment report
The 7-day recency exclusion means very new attachments require a manual re-trigger after the window passes
No notification or alert when migration completes or when an attachment fails repeatedly
documents.document exclusion is opportunistic (module presence check) but has no UI to override it
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['cloud.storage.migration.report'].search_read([], limit=10)  # per-model attachment stats
odoo shell: env['ir.config_parameter'].sudo().get_param('cloud_storage_migration_max_attachment_id')  # stable ceiling set at first run
odoo shell: env['ir.attachment'].sudo()._cron_migrate_local_to_cloud_storage()  # trigger migration directly (runs on shell = cron context)

open_questions: What cloud storage providers are supported by the cloud_storage parent module (e.g. S3, GCS, Azure Blob) — the upload method/URL shape depends on _generate_cloud_storage_upload_info which is not in this module.
Whether the 7-day recency exclusion window is configurable anywhere, or fixed in code.
Behaviour when the same attachment has been partially uploaded (upload succeeded but the write(type='cloud_storage') rolled back) — does the cloud object end up orphaned?
